data.hypothesis: The serial r-k-c variant measured 0.076396257 s, while row-parallel r-k-c without explicit SIMD measured 0.009476691 s. SIMD and k-unrolling follow-ups measured 0.010415142 s and 0.009647238 s, so this candidate keeps the plain contiguous row update and tests one contrasting change: initialize each C row inside its statically assigned row iteration instead of using a separate serial memset. This may improve output first-touch locality or have no benefit; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Keep SIMD and unrolling out of this initialization experiment so their prior slower results do not confound the comparison.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured row-parallel r-k-c candidate without SIMD was faster than the tested row-parallel SIMD and unrolled-SIMD candidates; the results do not establish why those variants were slower.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: If this candidate is not faster, retain the best measured row-parallel plain r-k-c variant and test other changes separately.

data.notes: The candidate initializes every output element on every call, then accumulates k in ascending order. The inner c loop retains contiguous B/C traversal without an explicit SIMD directive or unrolling. The worker count is capped at min(threads, N), with a single-thread path when the caller supplies at most one thread. No new correctness or timing results are claimed; compare controller checks for all official sizes and repeated native n=1024 timings. The catalog reports seven distinct measured programs and no repeated programs; this is a separate initialization variant rather than a renamed candidate.
transformations: Remove the separate serial memset and initialize each output row to zero inside the iteration that owns that row.
Parallelize independent rows with static OpenMP scheduling, capped at min(threads, N).
Retain ascending-k accumulation and contiguous c traversal; do not add explicit SIMD or unrolling.
